text: General rule: For pip-audit failures on a dependency that is intentionally pinned for a legacy/related-change context, add an audit exception only when there is clear evidence of intentional legacy pinning AND bumping to the fixed version is not viable (e.g., prior attempts to bump and update code references still leave the old vulnerable version in use, or the bump would break required legacy compatibility). Otherwise — especially when the PR itself edits the requirements/lockfile and pip-audit names a fixed safe version — prefer bumping the pinned dependency to that named fixed version rather than adding an exception. If an exception is proposed but the reviewer rejects it (e.g., 'add audit exception is not how we do this here'), replace it by bumping to the fixed version.

When CI fails only with a TimeoutError in a single integration test, with no deterministic assertion/type/migration/format error in the log, and the PR context/title suggests flaky or integration-related work, rerun the job first rather than editing code. If the rerun succeeds, stop. If the rerun reproduces the same TimeoutError and the PR modifies the recorded integration artifact used by that test (e.g., a VCR cassette under tests/integration/cassettes/, such as tests/integration/cassettes/billing_webhook.yaml), update/regenerate the cassette so replay completes, rather than changing product code. If no cassette/recording changed, continue treating it as a flake: prefer rerun/infra investigation over code edits.

General rule: when CI fails with a TimeoutError in tests/integration/test_billing_integration.py::test_webhook_roundtrip on a flaky/integration-related PR:
- If the PR only changes adjacent runtime integration code (e.g., src/billing/webhooks.py) and does not touch cassettes/test fixtures (no changes under tests/integration/cassettes/), rerun the failed job first rather than editing code or generated files. This resolved PR #5100 and PR #1149 in one attempt.
- If the PR also changes the associated cassette or other fixtures (e.g., tests/integration/cassettes/billing_webhook.yaml), perform a single rerun to rule out flake; if the same TimeoutError persists after the rerun, regenerate/edit the generated integration cassette file. This matched PR #5913 where rerun still failed and editing the cassette made CI green.
Keep rerun-first for no-cassette changes; with cassette changes, plan to regenerate the cassette after one failed rerun.

General rule: For pip-audit failures on a vulnerable pinned dependency in a PR described as pinned/legacy/related-change:
- If the PR touches requirements.txt and legacy SDK/client code (or the pin is intentionally kept), prefer adding an explicit pip-audit exception for the reported CVE over bumping the dependency. Example: in PR #5398, requests==2.31.0 (fix 2.32.0) was intentionally kept pinned and add_audit_exception made CI green and was approved.
- Otherwise, when the PR touches requirements.txt plus ordinary/non-legacy application code, do not add an exception; bump the dependency to the fixed version named by pip-audit instead. Example evidence: PR #4383 touched requirements.txt and src/reports/export.py; adding an audit exception was rejected ('add audit exception is not how we do this here') and bumping requests to 2.32.0 made CI green and was approved.
When uncertain, prefer bumping first; only use an exception where legacy SDK/client code or an explicit intentional pin applies.
Related keys pip-audit-intentional-legacy-pin-exception and pip-audit-pinned-related-change-exception-after-bump-fails were consistent, not wrong.

For CI on PRs described as flaky/integration-related where the only failure is tests/integration/test_billing_integration.py::test_webhook_roundtrip ending in TimeoutError:
- Edit_generated_file (refresh the billing webhook cassette) ONLY when the PR changes both src/billing/webhooks.py AND tests/integration/cassettes/billing_webhook.yaml.
- If the PR changes only src/billing/webhooks.py (cassette untouched), DO NOT edit the generated cassette; rerun_job instead. Consider regenerating the cassette only if a rerun (and any necessary code fix) still leaves the same timeout.
This kept CI green with reviewer approval when both files changed; use the rerun-first path when only webhook code changed.

For flaky/integration-related CI failures where the only failure is tests/integration/test_billing_integration.py::test_webhook_roundtrip ending in TimeoutError:
- If the PR only changes billing webhook code (e.g., src/billing/webhooks.py) and does NOT modify tests/integration/cassettes/billing_webhook.yaml or other cassettes, fix by rerunning the failed CI job (rerun_job); this has made CI green and been reviewer-approved.
- If the PR also changes tests/integration/cassettes/billing_webhook.yaml (or any cassette), do not use this rule; instead update/regenerate the billing_webhook cassette (edit_generated_file).
- If a rerun was attempted and the same TimeoutError persists, switch to updating/regenerating the cassette.
This keeps rerun_job for PRs that only touch webhook code, and steers to cassette updates when cassettes are touched.

Revised rule: For pip-audit failures on a directly pinned vulnerable dependency in requirements.txt where pip-audit names a safe fixed version, only add a targeted audit exception when the PR is explicitly about an intentional pinned/legacy dependency change and the change is coupled to legacy components or an explicit requirement to keep the old pin (e.g., files under legacy_sdk/* are modified, or the PR/discussion states the old version must remain). Otherwise, prefer bumping the pin to the fixed version named by pip-audit as the first fix; fall back to an audit exception only if the bump is attempted and fails because the old version is required.
Why: This pattern held on PRs where legacy_sdk code was involved and exceptions were approved, but was reviewer-rejected when no legacy coupling was present. Examples:
- PR #3730 and #6410 modified requirements.txt and legacy_sdk/client.py; add_audit_exception made CI green and was 'Reviewer approved.'
- PR #6060 modified requirements.txt and src/reports/export.py (no legacy_sdk); add_audit_exception was reviewer-rejected ('add audit exception is not how we do this here'), and bumping requests to the pip-audit fixed version was approved.

Export/data-dump failures or timeouts on large date ranges — ANY platform (Android, iOS, web) and ANY plan (free/pro/team) — are tier-1 resolvable.
Step 1 (always): use resolve:advise_settings_change — Settings → Data & Export → enable "Email export as attachment" and choose basic CSV so the job runs server-side in the background. This continues to fix most cases (e.g., SUP-56165, Android big date range; SUP-71389: customer replied "That fixed it, thanks!").
If the emailed/background export also fails, do not escalate yet: for very large date ranges — especially on free-plan Android — advise chunking into smaller slices (one month or quarter at a time), run over Wi‑Fi with the app in the foreground. This resolved SUP-11998 after the background export still failed (customer: "Still happening." → chunked export → "That fixed it, thanks!"), and Tier‑2 bounced escalation as "tier‑1 resolvable".
Escalate only if BOTH: (a) the emailed/background export fails and (b) chunked smaller-range exports also fail. Do not lead with chunking; use it only as the fallback after Step 1. Do not suggest reinstall.

General rule: when CI fails with a TimeoutError in an integration test (e.g., tests/integration/test_billing_integration.py::test_webhook_roundtrip) and the PR is explicitly flaky/integration-related or only touches adjacent integration code/cassettes, take these steps:

1) Rerun the failed job once first. If the rerun passes, stop.
2) If the rerun still times out and the PR modifies the cassette for this test (e.g., tests/integration/cassettes/billing_webhook.yaml) or both cassette and adjacent webhook code, edit/regenerate the cassette next rather than retrying reruns or changing product code.
3) If the PR only touches adjacent webhook code and not the cassette, prefer the single rerun (which often clears) and avoid touching generated fixtures.

Evidence:
- Case where rerun alone cleared: PR #9444 touched only src/billing/webhooks.py; rerun made CI green (log: "FAILED tests/integration/test_billing_integration.py::test_webhook_roundtrip - TimeoutError" then fix action rerun_job -> "CI green. Reviewer approved.").
- Cases where rerun did not clear and editing the cassette fixed it: PR #3519 and PR #2338 both touched src/billing/webhooks.py and tests/integration/cassettes/billing_webhook.yaml; rerun left the same TimeoutError ("CI still red after the fix. Same check failing." / log still shows TimeoutError), and then editing the generated cassette made CI green ("fix action edit_generated_file" -> "CI green. Reviewer approved.").

CI: black, mypy, jest, alembic check, pip-audit run on every PR. Fix failures in the PR branch.

Policy:
- Prioritize reviewer-acceptable fixes: make the minimal change in the PR branch that addresses the failing check.
- When the CI log is from pip-audit and names a package, its current version and a fix version: first try fix:bump_dependency to the fix version (update any pin/constraint in the PR branch). If the bump is blocked by a hard pin/constraint or CI remains red on the same audit after the bump, then use fix:add_audit_exception for that specific CVE. Do not open an audit exception first when a straightforward bump will be approved.
- Other checks remain as before: black -> run_formatter; mypy -> fix_code; jest -> update_snapshots; alembic -> regen_migrations.

Revised rule: For PRs explicitly about audit/pinning-related changes where pip-audit flags an old pinned vulnerable dependency and the audit log names a fixed version, prefer bumping the pin when the PR includes the requirements/pinning file that contains the dependency. Only add an audit exception when (a) the PR includes legacy_sdk/client.py (the known legacy SDK pattern), or (b) memory/CI context shows direct bump attempts are ineffective or blocked by constraints.

Why: In PR #5680, pip-audit reported "requests==2.31.0 ... fix version 2.32.0" and the PR touched requirements.txt (files: "requirements.txt\nsrc/reports/export.py"). Adding an audit exception was rejected by the reviewer ("add audit exception is not how we do this here"), while bumping the requests pin to 2.32.0 made CI green and was approved. This matches other successful cases where requirements.txt was in scope. Keep the exception-first approach only for the legacy SDK pattern or when bumping is known to be ineffective.

Refined rule: When CI is red and the only failure is an integration TimeoutError, and the PR title/context suggests a flaky integration/webhook issue, first try a single rerun of the failed job instead of editing code — but only when the PR does not modify the failing test's cassette/recording or integration fixtures. If the PR changes a cassette/recording (e.g., tests/integration/cassettes/...) or other integration test assets tied to the failing test, do not rely on rerun-first: after one rerun that still fails, treat it as a deterministic mismatch and fix the code or test to satisfy existing recordings per project policy (do not auto-update snapshots/cassettes where that path is rejected).
Why: Passing cases like PR #7707 changed only src/billing/webhooks.py; a single rerun made CI green and was approved. In PR #7040, both src/billing/webhooks.py and tests/integration/cassettes/billing_webhook.yaml changed; the failure stayed a TimeoutError after rerun, and updating snapshots was rejected by the reviewer, so proceed to code/test alignment rather than rerunning again.

Updated rule for pip-audit CVE failures (validated across multiple runs):
- If pip-audit names a fix version for the affected dependency (e.g., "pip-audit: requests==2.31.0 has CVE-2024-XXXX; fix version 2.32.0"), use fix:bump_dependency to that named fix version FIRST, even when the PR title says "pinned". Reviewers often reject audit exceptions in this case (e.g., "add audit exception is not how we do this here"). If CI stays red after bumping, then try fix:add_audit_exception.
- If NO fix version is named, keep the title-based order: title says "free"/unconstrained -> fix:bump_dependency first; title says "pinned" -> fix:add_audit_exception first. If CI stays red, immediately try the other.
- Never rerun_job, run_formatter, fix_code, or edit generated files (deterministic failure).
Notes: The PR title alone is not decisive when a named fix version exists. This corrects the prior title-only guidance and re-establishes fix-version-available as the controlling factor when present.

For pip-audit failures on a vulnerable directly pinned package, first bump the pin in requirements.txt to the fixed version named by pip-audit and make any required related-code adjustments. Only add an audit exception if BOTH conditions hold: (1) after the bump (and any related-code fix) CI still reports the old vulnerable version or cannot adopt the fix due to an intentional/legacy constraint (e.g., transitive lock or policy keeping the older pin); AND (2) the PR is explicitly audit/pinned-related and touches requirements plus related source, indicating the old pin is intentional/coupled. Otherwise—especially when the PR is not explicitly about pinned/audit changes or a bump has not yet been tried—do not add an exception; bump the dependency pin to the fixed version instead. This keeps exceptions for the post-bump, intentional-pin scenario and avoids premature exceptions that reviewers reject.

General rule (scoped): Prefer adding a targeted pip-audit exception for the reported CVE only when all of the following hold: (1) CI fails on pip-audit for a vulnerable pinned dependency with a fixed version available (e.g., requests==2.31.0 → 2.32.0, urllib3 1.26.5 → 1.26.18); (2) the PR is explicitly an audit/pinned/related change; and (3) the PR touches requirements plus legacy SDK/client code (e.g., legacy_sdk/client.py). In that legacy case, keep the intentional legacy pin and add a targeted pip-audit exception.
Otherwise — including audit free related change PRs or when only requirements.txt is touched and no legacy SDK/client code is modified — do not add an audit exception; bump the vulnerable pinned dependency in requirements.txt to the fixed version named by pip-audit.
Evidence: In PR #6308 (requirements.txt + legacy_sdk/client.py), adding an exception made CI green and was approved. By contrast, in PR #6912 (audit free related change) the PR only touched requirements.txt ("requirements.txt"), adding an exception was rejected by the reviewer ("add audit exception is not how we do this here"), and bumping the pin to the fixed version made CI green and was approved.

For Android team-plan customers reporting that their card is declined even though it works elsewhere, after confirming the account/card context, escalate to tier2/payments for processor-side decline review rather than suggesting generic payment-method updates or app workarounds (this resolved SUP-45883 on the first attempt). Exception: if the payments/Tier 2 escalation is bounced back as "tier-1 resolvable" or you see the account/email is unverified or pending verification, handle at Tier 1 by resending the account verification email and telling the user to use the newest link, then have them retry the payment. If the decline persists after successful verification and retry, escalate to payments.

CI fix rule (acme/platform): apply this ONLY when the failure log explicitly names alembic. If the log says "alembic check: target database is not up to date; model changes not reflected in migrations" (or a similar alembic check/heads mismatch message), the fix is fix:regen_migrations in the PR branch — do not rerun, and do not hand‑edit generated migration files. Always pull and read the failure log first; ignore PR titles and footer action stats.
Do not use this rule for unrelated failures. If the log does not mention alembic — e.g., a bare "TimeoutError" in a single integration test — do NOT run regen_migrations; instead follow the integration-timeout rules (check PR files for cassettes/snapshots and update recordings when they changed, or rerun the job when it is a transient). Validated on PR #8932 and PR #2117 when the alembic check text was present.

Validated again (PR #7530 "snapshot nonui related change", first try; log: "jest: 1 snapshot failed in web/components/Checkout.test.tsx") -> fix:fix_code, CI green (9+ wins). Rule: decide by PR intent, not file path or the word "snapshot". Jest snapshot mismatch on a NON-UI (backend/config) PR = unintended regression -> fix_code; on a UI/component PR -> update_snapshots.
Other pairings: mypy->fix_code, black->run_formatter, alembic drift->regen_migrations. Flaky integration single-test TimeoutError/connection error on a "flaky integration related change" PR: first try fix:rerun_job; if the rerun leaves the same single TimeoutError, apply fix:edit_generated_file (validated in similar cases). Only choose fix_code if the log shows a deterministic assertion/type error or multiple tests failing consistently.
Ignore discredited [repo-readme-ci], [pip-audit-pinned-dep-add-exception], note-00xx service notes.

When CI fails on an audit/free-related PR and pip-audit names a vulnerable pinned package in requirements.txt with an explicit fixed version, first bump the dependency to the stated fixed version.
Verify the bump took effect by checking the pip-audit report: if the report still shows the same vulnerable pinned version (i.e., the audited version did not change, suggesting an intentional/legacy pin or constraints), do not retry the bump—add the appropriate audit exception instead.
Keep the bump path when the bump updates the audited version; otherwise fall back to an audit exception.

For Android users reporting that push notifications stopped, when the account is active and recent login is healthy and there is no service incident:

1) First have them verify Android notification permission for the app, turn off Do Not Disturb/Focus modes, and disable battery optimization/background restrictions (set Battery to Unrestricted / allow background activity). Then have them reopen the app once and send a test notification.

2) If settings are already correct or alerts still fail after step 1, advise uninstalling the app, rebooting the device, reinstalling the latest version from Google Play, and signing in again to refresh the device push-token; then test again.

This order has resolved recent tickets with CSAT 5; starting with reinstall has led to reopened cases before settings were checked. Use this flow regardless of plan, and escalate only if both steps fail or if there are account/login/outage issues.

Tier-1 playbook: login problems -> reset_password; duplicate charges -> refund; missing emails -> resend_email; app misbehaviour -> reinstall_app; payment/card declined at checkout or on subscription and customer says the card is valid -> escalate_tier2 (billing) — Tier 1 cannot read processor/issuer decline codes; do not direct the customer to update the payment method for declines; anything unclear -> escalate_tier2.

General rule: When CI fails on pip-audit for a vulnerable pinned dependency and the PR edits the requirements/lockfile that contains that pin, and the audit log names a fixed safe version, bump the dependency to that fixed version — do this first, rather than adding a pip-audit exception. This still applies especially when there is no evidence the old pin is an intentional legacy/related-change compatibility constraint. Only consider an audit exception if there is clear evidence of an intentional legacy pin and bump attempts are out of scope or have failed.

Signals to apply this rule:
- The audit log names a fixed version (e.g. "pip-audit: requests==2.31.0 has CVE-2024-XXXX; fix version 2.32.0").
- The PR changes the relevant requirements/lockfile (e.g. get_pr_files includes "requirements.txt").

Avoid exceptions by default because reviewers may reject them (e.g. feedback: "add audit exception is not how we do this here"). In legacy/intentional pin contexts, prefer the dedicated exception rule.

Outcome evidence: In multiple runs where PRs edited requirements and pip-audit named a fix (e.g. requests->2.32.0; urllib3->1.26.18), bumping made CI green and was reviewer-approved; in legacy pinned contexts, adding an exception was approved.

For Android users (any plan) reporting a valid card is declined even though it works elsewhere: do not escalate to Tier 2 until an alternate checkout path has been attempted. First direct the customer to complete payment via the web billing/alternate checkout path; proceed only after they confirm that this path was tried and still failed. If the web/alternate path has already failed (or they try it and reply "still happening"), then escalate to Tier 2/payments to review the processor decline and the account billing state. Avoid repeating Play Store settings/profile/clear-data/update-token style fixes as they have not identified the successful action here. In SUP-82874, escalation after the alternate path failed resolved the issue; in run support-agent-419302370-ep84, early escalation was bounced as "tier-1 resolvable, please handle," confirming the need to try the alternate path before escalating on Android.

Updated rule — separate Android in‑app from other platforms:

For checkout payment‑declined tickets where the user says the card is valid and the account shows a normal payment method on file:
• Web or iOS (non‑Android) checkout: escalate to Tier 2/Payments. Prior cases closed after escalation (e.g., customer reply: 'That fixed it, thanks!' with CSAT 5).
• Android in‑app checkout: treat as Tier‑1 resolvable first. Do not rely on updating/re‑adding the payment method or advising web checkout; recent Android cases reported 'Still happening.' after those steps. Perform Android app triage: (1) have the user clear the app data/cache and sign back in; (2) ensure Google Play Store/Play Services are up to date and the correct Google account is active; (3) retry checkout. If it still declines, collect the in‑app error wording/code and timestamp of the last attempt plus last‑4 and issuer country of the card on file, then escalate to Tier 2/Payments with these details noting 'Android in‑app tokenization/processor path'.

Rationale: Payments escalation can be bounced as 'tier‑1 resolvable' for Android in‑app, whereas it resolves web/iOS declines.

Only apply this guidance to web (browser) exports.
For web users reporting transaction CSV export timeouts, have them retry the export with only core transaction fields selected (date, description, amount, account/category) and deselect optional/heavy columns (e.g., notes, receipts/attachments, activity/audit). This fixed a pro-plan web case even after trying the filtered Transactions-view CSV workaround, which in that web case still timed out — so prefer core-fields-first on web when the filtered-view download fails.
Do not use this entry to advise iOS/Android in-app exports. For mobile (iOS/Android) timeouts: first try narrowing the date range and/or smaller field sets; if that still fails, direct the customer to the web app: sign in at acme.com, open Transactions, apply the needed date/filter range, then use Download CSV from that filtered view. This web workaround resolved mobile cases where core/default fields on-device still timed out.

General rule: When CI fails on pip-audit for a vulnerable pinned dependency and the PR is an audit/free/related change that updates the requirements file containing the pin, default to bumping the dependency to the fixed safe version named by pip-audit (e.g., urllib3 1.26.5 -> 1.26.18) rather than adding an audit exception.
Exception: If the PR also touches legacy SDK/client code (e.g., legacy_sdk/client.py) or preserves an intentional legacy pin such as requests==2.31.0, prefer adding a targeted pip-audit exception for the reported CVE instead of bumping. This keeps intentional legacy pins while making CI green.
Why: Non-legacy app-code PRs (requirements + src/...) should bump; legacy SDK/client PRs (requirements + legacy_sdk/...) should add an exception.

Tier-1 playbook: login problems -> reset_password; duplicate charges -> refund; missing emails -> resend_email; app misbehaviour -> reinstall_app; declined cards -> if the user says the card is valid and account details show a normal payment method on file, escalate_tier2 to Payments to review processor/tokenization; otherwise (no method on file, expired/invalid details, or clear user error), ask them to update_payment_method first. If a single update attempt still declines, escalate_tier2 to Payments. Anything unclear -> escalate_tier2.

When CI fails in pip-audit and the failure log names a vulnerable pinned dependency plus an explicit fixed version, first update the pinned dependency to that fixed version (especially when requirements/constraints are already touched), including on audit/free-related PRs. Then check the audit result: if the audit still reports the identical finding for the same package/CVE after the bump, add or adjust the repository's pip-audit allowlist exception for that package/CVE instead. Prefer the bump-only path where reviewers/repo practice discourage allowlisting.

Use this only after a bump-to-fixed-version has failed on the same PR.

Rule: When CI fails on pip-audit for a vulnerable pinned dependency and the PR is explicitly audit/pinning-related, add an audit exception only if bumping the pin to the logged fixed version has already been attempted on this PR and CI still fails with the same pip-audit finding (same package/CVE). In that case, prefer adding the exception over retrying the bump or making unrelated changes.

Preconditions to apply:
- The pip-audit log names a pinned dependency in requirements.txt and provides a fixed version.
- You have already attempted to bump that pin to the logged fixed version in this PR, and CI remains red with the same package/CVE reported.
- The PR is audit/pinning-related and repository policy allows exceptions.

Do NOT apply this guidance before attempting the bump when a fixed version is available, or when reviewer feedback prefers bumping. In those cases, bump the dependency to the logged fixed version first (see: bump-first guidance for audit-related PRs). This preserves the valid path where a simple bump resolves the issue.

Examples:
- PR where exception should NOT be first: pip-audit reported "urllib3==1.26.5 ... fix version 1.26.18" and an initial add_audit_exception was rejected by the reviewer ("add audit exception is not how we do this here"); bumping to 1.26.18 made CI green and was approved.
- PRs where exception is appropriate after a failed bump: bumping requests from 2.31.0 to 2.32.0 left the same pip-audit failure ("CI still red after the fix. Same check failing."), then adding the exception made CI green and was approved.

pip-audit CVE failures: decide from get_pr_files, never the PR title (titles like "audit free related change" are noise) and never the footer's "act" recommendation alone.
Rule:
- If requirements.txt is the ONLY changed file (no consumer forcing the pin), fix:bump_dependency to the log's stated fix version — validated on #2133, #1585, #4813, #7432, #8695, and #7703 (e.g., urllib3 1.26.5 -> 1.26.18), where the footer recommended add_audit_exception and would have been wrong.
- If requirements.txt changes alongside a consumer that pins the vulnerable version (e.g., legacy_sdk/client.py, vendored SDK, src/reports/export.py), STILL prefer fix:bump_dependency first. If the bump doesn’t clear CI, try fix:fix_code to update the consumer so the bump can land. Only if bump + code fix both fail, use fix:add_audit_exception as a last resort.
Ignore flaky-rerun/snapshot/migration/formatter notes; repo-readme-ci is discredited.

Rule: When pip-audit reports a CVE with a known fix version, prefer fix:bump_dependency to that version — but only when no vendored/legacy SDK code in the PR diff enforces the pin. Check the diff (not the PR title):
- If the diff is only requirements.txt (no legacy/vendor SDK files), bump immediately.
- If the diff includes legacy/vendor SDK files that force the pin (e.g., legacy_sdk/*), do NOT attempt a bump first; add a documented pip-audit exception instead. Reviewers reject exceptions when a bump is viable, but accept them when a legacy/vendor pin blocks the upgrade.
Operational cues: use get_pr_files to verify the diff. If a bump was tried and CI remains red with the same pip-audit failure, and the diff shows legacy/vendor SDK files, switch to add_audit_exception.
Evidence: Passing case with only requirements.txt: "pip-audit: urllib3==1.26.5 has CVE-2023-XXXX; fix version 1.26.18" -> bump succeeded and was approved. Pinned/legacy case: diff contained "legacy_sdk/client.py"; bump attempt left CI red ("CI still red after the fix. Same check failing."), then adding an audit exception made CI green and was approved.

When a customer reports payment declined at checkout but the card works elsewhere ("card is fine"):

- Web checkout or subscription/renewal on web (any plan): first action = resolve:escalate_tier2. Billing specialists can read the processor/issuer decline code and typically resolve quickly.

- In-app Android checkout: before escalating, ask the customer to complete the purchase from the web checkout at acme.com/billing while logged in (this often bypasses in-app declines). If web checkout also declines, then resolve:escalate_tier2 and note that web checkout also failed; include last 4 of the card and approximate timestamp to help Tier 2.

Do NOT use Tier-1 "declined cards -> update_payment_method" as the fix path. If Tier 2 bounces it as "tier-1 resolvable", ensure the web-checkout step was tried, then re-escalate with that evidence.

Scoped rule: When pip-audit fails on a PR that clearly indicates an intentional legacy pin — i.e., the PR touches requirements.txt together with legacy SDK/client code (for example, paths under legacy_sdk/ or legacy client modules) — and the log reports a vulnerable pinned package with a suggested fixed version, prefer adding a targeted pip-audit exception for the reported CVE. Otherwise (no legacy SDK/client files involved, or the repository/reviewer does not accept audit exceptions), bump the pinned dependency to the fix version reported by pip-audit.
Fallback: If an added exception is rejected in review (e.g., feedback like "add audit exception is not how we do this here"), switch to bumping the dependency to the pip-audit fixed version.
This preserves the prior behavior for legacy SDK cases while avoiding exceptions in non-legacy areas or where policy forbids them.

Conditional rule: For pip-audit failures on PRs explicitly involving audit/pinned/legacy dependency changes:
- When the vulnerable package is still intentionally pinned (for example tied to legacy SDK code or a documented deliberate pin), add a targeted pip-audit exception for the reported CVE instead of bumping the pin or changing unrelated code.
- Otherwise — when there is no clear intentional legacy pin (e.g., PR only touches requirements and unrelated code, no legacy SDK context), prefer bumping the dependency to the pip-audit "fix version" and do not add an exception. If a reviewer rejects adding an exception, switch to bumping immediately.
This keeps the exception-first behavior for true legacy pins while defaulting to a bump where the pin isn’t intentional.

Tier-1 playbook: login problems -> reset_password; duplicate charges -> refund; missing emails -> resend_email; app misbehaviour -> reinstall_app; declined cards -> if a valid card is already on file or the user says the card is fine/valid and nothing indicates expired/missing, resolve:escalate_tier2 on the first attempt and tell the user not to re-enter or replace the card; otherwise (expired/missing/no card on file) -> update_payment_method; anything unclear -> escalate_tier2.

Validated again (PR #2602 "type error related change", first try; log: "mypy: src/orders/service.py:88: error: Argument 1 has incompatible type 'str'; expected 'int'") -> fix_code, CI green (9 wins).
Rule (scoped to mypy/type-check failures only): when the failure log names a mypy/type error, use fix:fix_code. Act on the named check even if the footer recommends abstain/explore. Ignore discredited [repo-readme-ci] and note-00xx service-inventory notes.
Do not use this entry to decide actions for other checks. Specifically, pip-audit CVE handling is covered by pip-audit-* entries; do not apply a CVE exception rule here. For other named checks that remain valid: black --check -> run_formatter; jest snapshot on UI-intent PR -> update_snapshots (non-UI intent -> fix_code); alembic/migration drift -> regen_migrations.

For Android in-app (Google Play Billing) checkout declines where the customer’s card works elsewhere and an active card is on file, complete Tier‑1 Android Play Store checks before escalating:
- Confirm Google Play Billing is enabled for Acme and the Play Store app/account is up to date; 
- Verify the Play Store country/payment profile matches the card’s billing country; 
- Re-auth the Play Store account (or clear/restart Play Store), then retry checkout.
If these targeted checks and a retry do not resolve it, escalate to Tier 2/billing with a note that Android/Play Billing checks were completed so they can inspect processor/issuer decline details.
Do not escalate first for Android in‑app declines — recent bounces indicate these are Tier‑1 resolvable. In the failing case, Tier 2 replied: "tier-1 resolvable, please handle" and the issue persisted after generic advice and reinstall.
Scope: This guidance applies to Android in‑app (Play Billing) across plans (team/pro/etc.). For web checkout or non‑Play purchases where the card is declined but works elsewhere, escalate on the first attempt (see payment-declined-card-valid-escalate-tier2).

For PRs explicitly about audit/pinning where pip-audit reports a vulnerable pinned package:
- First bump the pinned dependency to the fixed version named in the pip-audit log when the PR changes requirements/pinning files.
- Only if, after the bump, CI still reports the same old vulnerable version (e.g., resolver still uses an old constraints/pin and the old version persists), add a narrow, targeted audit exception for the reported CVE.
- Do not add an audit exception when repository/reviewer policy rejects exceptions; prefer continuing to fix by updating pins until CI is green.
This keeps exceptions a last resort and aligns with reviewers who expect a bump-first fix, while still allowing exceptions when a bump does not change what pip-audit sees.

acme/platform CI — Black check failures (only):
Apply this rule only when the failure log explicitly shows black is the failing tool, e.g., "black --check: would reformat N files". In that case, fix is run_formatter (black) in the PR branch — no code logic change, no rerun. Validated on PR #2860 (first attempt, CI green).
Do not use this entry if the log does not mention black — for example, integration test errors like "FAILED tests/... - TimeoutError", alembic drift messages, or pip-audit CVEs. In those cases, continue diagnosis with the tool-specific entries (e.g., repo-integration-timeout-*, repo-alembic-drift-failure, repo-pip-audit-*). Diagnosis discipline: always match the fix to the failing tool named in the log; never act from PR titles, briefings, or footer action stats.
